questions: Did the slalom progress rise above 0.51 (iteration 9) at base_speed 1.3, and did its line_loss_events fall toward 1.0?
Did the s-bend hold 18 or more finishes, with line_loss_events at or below 0.8 and steering_oscillation under about 0.35?
Did the oval hold 20 of 20 with max_error near 0.017?
If the slalom is still at its max_error floor with 0 finishes, is the next geometry step a wheel_track 0.095 trial?

intent: Hold the iteration 9 best geometry unchanged, so that the Integrator's base_speed 1.3 change is the only variable. Expect the oval to stay at 20 of 20 with max_error near 0.017, the s-bend to hold 18 or more finishes, and the slalom progress to rise above 0.34 if speed is limiting it. If the slalom gains come with the s-bend holding, geometry stays fixed. If the s-bend drops below 18 finishes, the speed cut is costing bend time.
learning: Iteration 9 showed that the controller change lifted slalom progress from 0.34 to 0.51 with the same geometry, so control is now the main lever on the slalom. Holding geometry fixed in this iteration isolates the speed effect. The result will show whether geometry is at its limit (no slalom gain at lower speed) or whether a speed trade is worth keeping. The next geometry move is conditional on that result, and wheel_track 0.095 is the candidate if the slalom stays stuck at its floor.
rationale: Iteration 9 (score 681.3) is the best measured result. Its geometry matches iteration 8: body_length 0.10, mass 0.6, sensors at y 0.075 with x at -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03, 12 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.09, wheel_radius 0.03. Across iterations 8 and 9 the oval held 20 of 20 finishes (max_error about 0.016), and the s-bend held 18 to 19 of 20 finishes. The slalom still has 0 finishes, but its progress rose from 0.34 to 0.51 with the controller change, so control, not geometry, is now moving the slalom. Iterations 5 to 7 showed that yaw inertia has reached its useful limit (mass 0.5 reversed the s-bend gain), and iteration 4 showed that the 16 mm footprint costs oval reliability. Geometry is therefore close to its limit. The Integrator's plan for this iteration lowers base_speed to 1.3 to test whether speed is the constraint. To read that result cleanly, I hold every geometric value at the iteration 8 and 9 setting and change nothing. If the slalom progress rises with the s-bend still at 18 or more finishes, geometry stays fixed. If the slalom stays at its max_error floor with 0 finishes, the next geometry trial is wheel_track 0.095, which trades s-bend progress for slalom retention, as the iteration 2 and 3 comparison suggested. I do not make a y 0.08 move now, because the Integrator's rule makes that conditional on a slalom gain at the lower speed.
